text:
To survive motherhood, find that one mom who matches your level of 🤪.

It's non-negotiable.

She's the person who reminds you that your house isn't the only one covered in Hot Wheels, snack crumbs, and questionable life choices. The one who makes you laugh so hard that you might pee a little (true story), and suddenly motherhood feels a whole lot lighter.

My long-distance bestie is a mom to a beautiful eight-year-old girl. As a mom of a three-year-old tornado, I get a glimpse into my future, along with survival tips for every new stage of parenting. It's comforting to know that someone has already survived the jungle I've only just entered.

Now, let's talk about work.

Motherhood comes with an impossible expectation: work like you don't have kids, and parent like you don't have a job. In my case, the biggest person putting that pressure on me... is me.

So when AI became part of my daily routine, I finally felt a little relief because it feels like having another bestie: one who's available 24/7 to challenge ideas, generate alternatives, and help me see things from a different perspective.

Do I have it all figured out? Absolutely f***ing not.

Most days, I'm overwhelmed by the amount of information about AI, trying to master Claude Design while simultaneously figuring out life with a threenager.

Sleep has become more of a concept than a habit.

But I've realized something. I'm not here to eliminate the chaos. I'm here to organize it in a way that works for this season of my life.

And everyone keeps telling me it gets easier. I'm choosing to believe them... and the calming pills, of course.
